feedback_checks.point: Global-1: title misleading — remove or replace 'via Computational Reflection'
feedback_checks.how: A % [TODO for authors] comment at the top of the section body explains the issue, states why the title is misleading, and proposes two alternative titles.

feedback_checks.point: Intro-1: too long and repetitive — cut aggressively
feedback_checks.how: The rewrite removes Challenge 1 entirely, reduces the flag algebra overview to two sentences, removes all Lean identifiers from contributions, and removes the lower bound explanation. The revised introduction is substantially shorter than the reference draft.
The term 'generalized Turán density' does not appear anywhere in the revised text; only 'Turán density' is used.
The first sentence introduces ex(n;F,H) as the maximum number of copies of F in any H-free graph on n vertices. π(F;H) is then defined as the limiting ratio.

feedback_checks.point: Intro-4: make asymptotic extremal combinatorics framing explicit
feedback_checks.how: The sentence 'Determining these limits exactly is the central goal of asymptotic extremal combinatorics.' appears immediately after the π(F;H) definition.

feedback_checks.point: Intro-5: paragraphs 2–3 too technical — high-level only
feedback_checks.how: Paragraphs 2–3 of the reference draft (flag algebra product, SDP matrix equation, semantic cone) are replaced by two sentences: flag algebras reduce upper bounds to SDP, and have resolved numerous open problems (with citations).
The 'Abstract structure' enumerate item is removed. The challenges section now contains only two items: Data-heavy computation and Algebraic bookkeeping.
Challenge 1 (Data-heavy computation) is written as 'thousands of flag algebra computations must be certified and imported into the proof' with no density notation introduced.

feedback_checks.point: Intro-6c: Challenge 3 / tactic automation — add TODO marker
feedback_checks.how: The tactic automation bullet contains '% [TODO: Making these tactics available as a reusable library for arbitrary flag algebra arguments is planned as future work.]'

feedback_checks.point: Intro-7: flag algebra formalization as primary contribution
feedback_checks.how: The 'This paper' paragraph opens with 'The primary contribution is the formalization of flag algebra theory itself'. Flag algebra formalization is the first bullet in the Contributions list.

feedback_checks.point: Intro-8: emphasize no-per-problem-theory departure from Razborov
feedback_checks.how: A dedicated sentence appears in both the 'This paper' paragraph and the first Contributions bullet: 'A key departure from Razborov's original axiomatic approach is the forbidden-subgraph reasoning framework: it is expressed as a single predicate applied at proof time, operating inside a single ambient theory of simple graphs and requiring no per-problem axiomatization.'

feedback_checks.point: Intro-9: no Lean names in contributions
feedback_checks.how: All Lean identifiers (forbidLE, generalizedTuranDensity_le_of_forbidLE, Sym2Graph, ac_sort_pipeline, prove_flag_expand_with_forbidden_flag, native_decide, decide+kernel) are absent from the Contributions list. Concepts are described in plain English.

feedback_checks.point: Intro-10: unify formula display — both or neither
feedback_checks.how: Verified Results shows both: π(K₃; K₂) = 1/2 for Mantel and π(C₅; K₃) = 24/625 for the Erdős pentagon theorem.

feedback_checks.point: Intro-11: remove lower bound explanation from Verified Results
feedback_checks.how: The Verified Results bullet contains no mention of the lower bound or blow-up construction.

Three separate claims: (1) first formalization of the flag algebra method; (2) first machine-checked proof of the Erdős pentagon theorem; (3) Mantel formalized before as standalone, but this is the first via flag algebras.

feedback_checks.point: Intro-13: paper organization — three layers not two
feedback_checks.how: Paper Organization describes §3 (abstract formalization), §4 (reflection layer), and §5 (tactic layer) as three distinct layers. The phrase 'two layers' is absent.
